intent: Record as reviewed the import ceiling, naming, provenance and version-admission rules the ingest Context enforces and tests but the Registry did not hold.
observable_outcome: get-context ingest lists the seven rules as reviewed, each citing its enforcing code and the test that proves it.

acceptance_criteria.statement: One import may create at most MaxSkillsPerImport (50) Skills; a source that would create more is refused as a whole, naming the count it would create and the ceiling. Skills refused for other reasons do not count.

When two directories of one source declare the same Skill name, the first keeps it and the later ones are refused with a duplicate-name finding naming the first path, instead of silently becoming its next version.

A Skill arriving from a plugin or URL is refused as name_held_by_another_source when the same-named Skill's latest version came from a different plugin or URL; the rest of the import proceeds. Uploads without an origin and generated sources are exempt.
A taken-down Skill refuses every new version as skill_taken_down and gains no version row; in a re-import of several Skills the others still import.
A new version must declare the same name as its Skill; another name is refused as version_name_mismatch and neither a version nor the summary changes.

A version is written only when its source carries the provenance its kind requires: git needs a URL and no generator fields, an upload has neither, a generated source needs a model and prompt version and no URL; anything else is refused with ErrIncompleteProvenance.
A name held by a generated Skill takes no uploaded version, and a generated candidate takes no name held by an uploaded Skill; either way the save is refused with ErrGeneratedNameCollision.
